content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To measure quality of life, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Design a pilot questionnaire (4 days)
Step 2. Recruit a focus group for preliminary testing (1 week)
Step 3. Compile a list of relevant socio-economic indicators (3 days)
Step 4. Finalize the survey methodology documentation (2 days)
Step 5. Clean the raw data collected from field agents (5 days)
Step 6. Select a representative geographic sample (2 days)
Step 7. Draft the final executive summary (1 day)
Step 8. Obtain ethical clearance from the review board (1 month)
Step 9. Verify the accuracy of household income reports (2 weeks)
Step 10. Define the operational boundaries of the study (1 week)
Step 11. Coordinate with local municipal leaders (4 days)
Step 12. Perform the primary statistical analysis (1 week)
Step 13. Secure funding for the large-scale data collection (2 months)
Step 14. Hire and train temporary field enumerators (10 days)
Step 15. Review existing literature on global happiness indices (2 weeks)
Step 16. Cross-reference survey results with census data (5 days)
Step 17. Draft the initial project proposal (1 week)
Step 18. Archive the raw interview recordings (2 days)
Step 19. Identify key stakeholders in the community (3 days)
Step 20. Determine the budget for digital tablet devices (4 days)
Step 21. Map out the logistical routes for the survey team (2 days)
Step 22. Conduct the door-to-door interviews (3 weeks)
Step 23. Encode the survey responses into a database (1 week)
Step 24. Conduct a small-scale trial run in one district (5 days)
Step 25. Backup all digital research files (1 hour)
Step 26. Analyze access to healthcare services (4 days)
Step 27. Evaluate the impact of environmental factors (6 days)
Step 28. Assess the reliability of the collected samples (3 days)
Step 29. Evaluate the educational attainment levels (1 week)
Step 30. Calculate the Gini coefficient for the region (2 days)
Step 31. Purchase necessary statistical software licenses (1 day)
Step 32. Distribute the final survey forms (2 days)
Step 33. Monitor data entry for clerical errors (4 days)
Step 34. Establish a secure server for data storage (3 days)
Step 35. Measure the average commute times (2 days)
Step 36. Review the nutritional standards of the population (1 week)
Step 37. Contact the graphic design team for layout (2 days)
Step 38. Calculate the life expectancy at birth (1 day)
Step 39. Evaluate the housing affordability index (5 days)
Step 40. Formulate the research questions (1 week)
Step 41. Apply for a government research grant (3 weeks)
Step 42. Audit the data collection process (4 days)
Step 43. Assess the availability of clean drinking water (1 week)
Step 44. Establish the criteria for "high quality" living (3 days)
Step 45. Set up a hotline for survey participant questions (2 days)
Step 46. Categorize the target demographic groups (4 days)
Step 47. Analyze the local employment rates (5 days)
Step 48. Create data visualization charts (3 days)
Step 49. Draft the policy recommendations section (4 days)
Step 50. Validate the phone numbers of respondents (2 days)
Step 51. Collect data on community safety and crime (1 week)
Step 52. Interview local business owners (3 days)
Step 53. Solicit feedback from independent observers (2 days)
Step 54. Organize a mid-project review meeting (1 day)
Step 55. Weight the data based on population density (3 days)
Step 56. Peer-review the preliminary findings (2 weeks)
Step 57. Compare results with neighboring regions (5 days)
Step 58. Perform a sensitivity analysis on the variables (2 days)
Step 59. Define the survey's margin of error (2 days)
Step 60. Check for statistical outliers in the data (3 days)
Step 61. Synthesize the findings into a comprehensive report (1 week)
Step 62. Verify the air quality index measurements (3 days)
Step 63. Assess the level of political freedom (4 days)
Step 64. Develop a scoring system for qualitative answers (1 week)
Step 65. Translate the survey into local languages (5 days)
Step 66. Present the findings to the city council (2 hours)
Step 67. Assemble the core research team (1 week)
Step 68. Search for historical quality of life benchmarks (3 days)
Step 69. Write the methodology section of the report (4 days)
Step 70. Identify the most vulnerable neighborhoods (2 days)
